fixedWEBChecks.text: Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, “As you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build him a house in which to dwell, so deal with me.
Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, “Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them.”

Huram continued, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who would build a house for the LORD and a house for his kingdom.
Now I have sent a skillful man, endowed with understanding, Huram-abi,

the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan; and his father was a man of Tyre. He is skillful to work in gold, in silver, in bronze, in iron, in stone, in timber, in purple, in blue, in fine linen, and in crimson, also to engrave any kind of engraving and to devise any device, that there may be a place appointed to him with your skillful men, and with the skillful men of my lord David your father.
Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Solomon in God’s house:
Huram-abi also made the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all its vessels for King Solomon, for the LORD’s house, of bright bronze.

primaryTextAssessment.2CH2:13-14: 2:13 explicitly names Huram-abi as the skilled man sent by the letter’s speaker; 2:14 continues with “He” and gives parentage/skills. The immediate antecedent is the artisan, not the king.
primaryTextAssessment.2CH4:11: Names Huram as maker of the pots, shovels and basins and says he finished the work for Solomon’s house. It does not state Huram-abi or bronze in this verse.
primaryTextAssessment.2CH4:16: Names Huram-abi again as maker of vessels for Solomon and the LORD’s house, specifying bright bronze. This supports linking the named artisan to 4:11, while the “Huram-abi” form and bronze detail are explicit here.
primaryTextAssessment.sameBookIdentity: Strongly supported, with an inference qualifier: the distinctive Huram/Huram-abi name, artisan role, Solomon’s temple project, and the immediately adjacent 4:11/4:16 work descriptions point to one artisan. The fixed WEB does not expressly say “the same Huram-abi who was sent in 2:13,” so record the cross-passage join as a reviewed same-person inference rather than a verbatim identification.
primaryTextAssessment.tyreKingSeparation: Keep person:hiram_1532 distinct. 2:3 identifies Huram as king of Tyre; 2:11–12 continue the king’s letter; 2:13 then says “I have sent” a skilled man, Huram-abi. The king is the sender and the artisan is the sent person.
primaryTextAssessment.genealogyAndTranslation: 2CH2:14 says the artisan’s mother is from Dan and his father is a man of Tyre. 1KI7:14 instead says a widow of Naphtali and a Tyrian father (kings1 witness SHA c72b757cd8a5266b615d91df7478e11bad5d951a662c091b875d62dae9b5d384). Preserve each book’s wording; do not harmonize the maternal tribal difference or treat it alone as proof of distinct artisans.

identityProposal.recommendedHandling: Treat person:huram_1575 (2:13–14) and person:hiram_1533 (4:11, 4:16) as likely the same artisan within 2 Chronicles, subject to integration adjudication. If the runtime must retain stable records, store an alias/same-person relation between these existing IDs rather than minting an ID. Keep the Tyre king as a distinct person.
identityProposal.confidence: high, but not explicit identity wording across the chapter boundary
reasons: Huram-abi is introduced as the sent skillful man at 2:13.
At 4:11 Huram completes the same Solomon-house work and makes utensils; 4:16 immediately names Huram-abi as making more vessels for Solomon’s house.
The artisan name and distinctive role align; 4:16 is direct evidence for the form “Huram-abi.”
limits: The article evidence is related-section only and does not establish identity.
Do not import the artisan’s wider 1 Kings mother-tribe wording into 2 Chronicles.
Do not import Masonic Hiram Abiff lore or treat it as biblical identity evidence.

displayGateProposal.at2CH2:13: If the existing Huram-abi profile is retained as the canonical display record, its name and safe description may begin at 2:13, because the artisan is named there. Keep 2:14 parentage and expanded skills gated at 2:14.
displayGateProposal.at2CH4:11: For the 4:11 use, show only “フラム” and the verse-supported work/finishing description. Do not expose the 4:16 bronze detail early. If the system keeps separate records until the alias resolution point, do not expose the “フラム・アビ” alias on the 4:11-only record before 4:16.
displayGateProposal.at2CH4:16: At 4:16, expose the explicit alias “フラム・アビ” on the 4:11 artisan record (or connect it to the existing 2:13 record), and only here expose the bright-bronze detail. If the records are unified, Huram-abi itself is already known at 2:13, but the 4:16 fact about bronze remains gated.
displayGateProposal.neverMerge: The Tyre king’s “Huram” name at 2:3/11/12 must remain separate from the artisan sent at 2:13.
